newsitem.title: USA: SEC revokes registration of A.R. Baron and Co Inc.
newsitem.headline: SEC revokes registration of A.R. Baron and Co Inc.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Thursday it revoked the registration of New York brokerage firm A .R. Baron and Co Inc and started administrative proceedings against other former officials.
The SEC moved against Andrew Bressman, Richard Acosta, Richard Simone, Mark Goldman alleging they committed fraud in violation of securities laws.
Bressman, one of Baron's top officer, Okin, Acosta and others allegedly manipulated the market for the common stock of Health Professionals Inc in May and June 1993, the commission said.
Bressman and Roman Okin, another Baron official, in 1995 allegedly manipulated the price of Cypros Pharmaceutical's common shares from January through October 1995.

Further, SEC said that in 1991, Bressman, Acosta and others as registered brokers with D.H. Blair and Co Inc allegedly manipulated the market for the common stock of Professional Care Inc, Health Professional's predecessor.
While Simone was at Baron, the SEC charged he allegedly placed large unauthorized trades in a customer's account and Goldman on several occasions, allegedly refused to carry out customer sell orders.
A.R. Baron had filed for bankruptcy protection in July after the SEC accused it of sales fraud. A trustee had been appointed to take control and liquidate Baron's assets.
The SEC ordered Baron to stop soliciting or carrying out security transactions for itself or its customers rather than liquidating customer positions.
Bressman and Okin also filed for bankruptcy protection in July. The bankruptcy court had prohibited the duo from using any property of the company.

The brokers hearing will take place before an administrative law judge. The location and date are yet to be determined. The administrative proceedings wil determine whether remedial action is appropriate.
The SEC would not say how much money was involved in these cases.
